answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it ran duplicate identities. Like a single ember in a tundra night, one honest identity stands out while fakes multiply cost — an attacker at the zenith of scale still pays a fresh bond per clone, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand deposits, and the honest majority keeps the registry trustworthy.
